entries.title: AI Film Festival Japan Draws 730 Entries From More Than 60 Countries | News On Japan
entries.paragraph_1:
TOKYO -
 The AI Film Festival Japan 2026, one of Asia's largest international film festivals dedicated to works created using artificial intelligence, held its awards ceremony in Tokyo on November 1, attracting more than 730 submissions from over 60 countries and regions, with short films and animation accounting for the majority of entries.
entries.paragraph_2: The festival, now in its second year, was first held in Tokyo in November 2025 and has expanded rapidly as advances in generative AI make sophisticated video production increasingly accessible to independent filmmakers and creators. As AI technology becomes more deeply integrated into everyday life, film festivals specializing in AI-generated content have emerged around the world, providing opportunities for artists to explore new forms of storytelling and visual expression. This year's festival, held from October 31 to November 2 at Tokyo Innovation Base in the Marunouchi district, attracted a diverse range of submissions, including narrative films, animation, experimental productions and works incorporating AI-generated music. From the more than 730 entries, organizers selected 68 works for official screening, with 21 advancing to the final round of judging. Japan, China and South Korea accounted for more than half of all submissions, highlighting East Asia's growing prominence in AI-assisted filmmaking. Most entries were short films or animated productions lasting approximately five to 10 minutes, reflecting the increasing popularity of compact storytelling formats among creators experimenting with generative video technology. Among the AI tools used by participants, Seedance, a video generation system developed by China's ByteDance, the company behind TikTok, was the most widely used. Suno, an AI music generation platform developed by the American company of the same name, ranked second, demonstrating the growing importance of AI-generated soundtracks and music in filmmaking. The increasing sophistication of these technologies has enabled individual creators and small production teams to produce films that previously required substantial budgets, specialized equipment and large crews. AI tools can now generate moving images, characters, backgrounds and musical compositions, allowing filmmakers to concentrate more heavily on storytelling, direction and creative concepts. Recognizing the expanding role of music in AI filmmaking, organizers introduced a new AI Film Music and Score category this year. The competition evaluated how effectively creators could use artificial intelligence to compose music that complemented visual sequences, emphasizing synchronization, musical quality and emotional impact. Ayano Kotakagari, a young creator at Nippon Television's production company NTV AX-ON, won the top award in the newly established category. The festival's founder and executive committee chairman, Kazunori Kurimoto, emphasized that technological advances alone would not determine the artistic quality of AI-generated films. Kurimoto said that although AI technology continues to evolve rapidly, the ultimate quality of a production depends on the creator's individual worldview, imagination and originality. His remarks reflected a central theme of the festival: while artificial intelligence is transforming how films are produced, the ability to develop compelling stories and distinctive artistic visions remains fundamentally dependent on human creativity.

entries.title: US, South Korea and Japan Renew Commitment to North Korea’s Denuclearization
entries.paragraph_1: The United States, South Korea and Japan have renewed their commitment to the “complete denuclearization” of North Korea as Pyongyang continues to reject disarmament ahead of possible nuclear talks with Washington. Speculation has grown over a possible meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during next month’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China, following repeated overtures by Trump for renewed nuclear negotiations. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi reaffirmed their position during a meeting on Friday on the sidelines of the Group of 20 (G20) gathering in Atlanta, Georgia. Advertisement According to the US State Department, the three officials “reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization” of North Korea. They also pledged to ensure the “full implementation” of United Nations Security Council resolutions, including measures prohibiting support for revenue-generating activities linked to North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. Despite years of international sanctions, North Korea, which enjoys support from Russia and China, has legally entrenched its status as a nuclear-armed state. Its government has repeatedly insisted that its nuclear arsenal is permanent and irreversible. Advertisement Trump open to meeting Kim Trump has repeatedly expressed willingness to engage Pyongyang in nuclear negotiations while reducing joint military exercises with South Korea, a key US ally. The US president departed from longstanding American policy last year when he acknowledged that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”. He also signalled that he was “100 percent” open to meeting Kim, although the North Korean leader did not respond to the proposal. Advertisement Analysts and South Korea’s intelligence agency believe Kim may have communicated Pyongyang’s position on possible talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong. South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung, who has adopted a more conciliatory approach towards Pyongyang, has repeatedly called for dialogue without preconditions. In September, Lee suggested that Washington consider pursuing a freeze on North Korea’s nuclear programme rather than demanding its immediate dismantlement, in exchange for sanctions relief. Advertisement However, critics argue that such a proposal could amount to tacit recognition of North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to secure sanctions relief without surrendering its weapons. Some analysts also believe China may be moving towards accepting North Korea’s nuclear status, citing the absence of references to denuclearisation in statements issued after Kim met Chinese President Xi Jinping in June. Meanwhile, Pyongyang on Saturday criticised a joint statement issued by a group of countries monitoring the implementation of sanctions against it. Advertisement North Korea insisted that “the stereotyped sanctions racket of the US and the West can neither influence the position of the DPRK (North Korea) as a nuclear weapons state”. entries.title: North Korea answers South’s proposal for military talks by firing off ballistic missiles
entries.paragraph_1: North Korea fired more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on Thursday, 17 days after its previous ballistic missile launch on Oct. 12. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the projectile launches from the Wonsan area around 12:30 pm. The launches came six days after South Korea’s Ministry of National Defense proposed military talks with North Korea on Oct. 23 to prevent accidental clashes along the Military Demarcation Line following recent land mine explosions in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). According to the Joint Chiefs, the missiles traveled around 250 kilometers. South Korean and US authorities are currently analyzing the technical details. The missiles were reportedly among a range of weapons systems — including 600 mm super-large multiple rocket launchers — that North Korean forces drilled on Thursday. South Korea’s National Security Office convened an emergency meeting with officials from the Defense Ministry, the Joint Chiefs and other relevant agencies to review the security situation. “We emphasized the need to thoroughly assess the implications of the launches for our security and ensure that all necessary measures are taken,” an office spokesperson said after the meeting. The office also urged North Korea to immediately halt its repeated ballistic missile launches, calling them “violations of UN Security Council resolutions and grave actions that do nothing to help contain the current situation.”

entries.title: North Korea answers South’s proposal for military talks by firing off ballistic missiles
entries.paragraph_1: North Korea fired more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on Thursday, 17 days after its previous ballistic missile launch on Oct. 12. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the projectile launches from the Wonsan area around 12:30 pm. The launches came six days after South Korea’s Ministry of National Defense proposed military talks with North Korea on Oct. 23 to prevent accidental clashes along the Military Demarcation Line following recent land mine explosions in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). According to the Joint Chiefs, the missiles traveled around 250 kilometers. South Korean and US authorities are currently analyzing the technical details. The missiles were reportedly among a range of weapons systems — including 600 mm super-large multiple rocket launchers — that North Korean forces drilled on Thursday. South Korea’s National Security Office convened an emergency meeting with officials from the Defense Ministry, the Joint Chiefs and other relevant agencies to review the security situation. “We emphasized the need to thoroughly assess the implications of the launches for our security and ensure that all necessary measures are taken,” an office spokesperson said after the meeting. The office also urged North Korea to immediately halt its repeated ballistic missile launches, calling them “violations of UN Security Council resolutions and grave actions that do nothing to help contain the current situation.”
entries.paragraph_2: By Jang Na-rye, staff reporter; Kwon Hyuk-chul, staff reporter

entries.title: Fate of Bay Area Public Transit Hinges on Regional Transit Measure | Post News Group
entries.paragraph_1: By Tanay Gokhale, Bay City News On Nov. 3, voters in five Bay Area counties will vote on a regional sales tax measure that, if it fails, could prompt local transit agencies to close train stations and cut bus service. If passed, the Regional Transit Measure, or RTM, will impose a half-cent sales tax in Alameda, Contra Costa, San Mateo, and Santa Clara counties as well as a one-cent sales tax in San Francisco starting April 2027. The tax would raise an estimated $980 million annually for 14 years to fund the region’s public transit agencies, which are struggling with massive financial deficits. Revenue would go to BART, Muni, Caltrain, Alameda-Contra Costa Transit, the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority, the San Francisco Bay Ferry, Golden Gate Transit, and other transportation agencies operating in the five counties. In California, a regional measure for a new sales tax would normally require a two-thirds majority approval if the state Legislature directly places it on a ballot. Transit advocates, however, chose to collect signatures to make the sales tax a citizen-initiated ballot measure that would lower the threshold to a simple majority of votes cast across the five counties.
